title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance annual rent increase cap
requirement: A landlord may not raise rent by more than the change in the Consumer Price Index, capped at 4% per year, and may not raise rent more than once in any 12-month period.
coverage_conditions: All multiple dwellings in Newark are subject to rent control; exempt are public housing, transient hotel/motel rooms, commercial space, newly constructed and vacant dwellings, and certain Section 8/rehabilitation or government-regulated units.

conditions.text: units rehabilitated under federal/state Rental Rehabilitation Programs receiving Section 8 subsidies or housing vouchers
units under a government contract that regulates rent (preempted during the contract)

coverage_quotes: All multiple dwellings, as defined in subsection 19:2-2, are subject to Rent Control pursuant to this Title XIX Rent Control
EXEMPTIONS — Shall mean dwellings to which this chapter shall not apply.

if the authority of that governmental agency supersedes the authority of the City of Newark to regulate such rents, then the application of this chapter shall be preempted during the period of governmental agency regulation specified in the contract.

exemptions: Public housing; transient hotel/motel space; commercial space; newly constructed and vacant dwellings; rehabilitated units receiving Section 8 or federal vouchers; units under a government rent-regulation contract while it is in force.
quoted_span: At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of the lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord may request or receive an increase greater than the percentage increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) from the CPI 15 months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase to the CPI three months prior to the month of the proposed rent increase. In no case shall the allowable rent increase exceed 4%.
interaction: Preempted by a government agency rent-regulation contract during its term; the chapter resumes when the contract ends.
